method: Executed production renderer with pixel-backed source sheets and captured actual drawImage transforms for every eye at its declared closed cel.
Compared the captured closed axis with canonical source geometry, upper-contour slope, arc endpoints, and common eye line.
Visually reviewed all 40 original faces. Recommendations separate circle-gap orientation from eyelid attitude; no original resting art was changed.

recommendations: Never apply a single zero-angle rule to all 80 eyes: angry hooks, tired crossbars, source closed arcs and bars have intentional attitudes.
Round eyes need independent screen-level blink coordinates; slot.rot and reference alignment encode circle-gap placement, not head tilt.
For source closed arcs, preserve concavity and endpoints in a squeeze. Several aligned arcs rotate roughly 160 to 180 degrees, which reverses generic lid curvature.
For hook eyes, derive a bounded target from the source upper lid, not the generic hook alignment.
Make closure angle approach its target during closing and undo it during reopening; prevent a sudden orientation jump when entering or leaving the closed frame.
Expression-transition closed bridges must use the same per-eye closure orientation as ordinary blinks.
limitations: This audit proposes art direction and identifies large rotation mismatches. It does not by itself certify natural motion.
PCA or whole-glyph alignment is unreliable for circular and asymmetric glyphs; source geometry measurements are supporting cues, not a complete automatic design rule.
